summary:
Through coord 0.112 and the 0.113 source of #4802, one passive association kept at most 8 source cursors and 256 response identities and never removed either. A new path past 8 gave `source-index-full-capture-deferred`; a pass whose new identities would exceed 256 set `response-index-full-capture-deferred` without advancing, so the same records were rescanned and deferred on every later pass. Measured 2026-10-23 on the fdev host (capture-only, no network): two real Claude Code 2.1.309 transcripts (0.98 MB subagent, 4.6 MB main) reached 235 observations in ten passes, and passes 11-16 all deferred. The host wrote about 152 transcripts in 24 hours (150 subagent files), so the association could not cover a reporting window. Any passive producer with many files or one long session hits this; it is not Claude-specific.

The fix (Outcome #4640, this revision) closes a source when a pass reads its descriptor to the end on a line boundary and the file has been unmodified for 15 minutes. The cursor moves to a compact retired entry and the source's identities leave the index. A later append resumes from the entry; a closed file whose anchor no longer matches is skipped (`closed-source-discontinuity-skipped`), never re-read from zero. An active Claude transcript keeps its newest 24 identities. At most 384 retired entries are kept; evicting the oldest sets a horizon one second after that file's modification time, and records at or before it from an unknown source are suppressed (`pre-horizon-record-suppressed`). Retirement travels in the existing intent as absolute values, so a crash applies it once.

Why re-emission must be prevented, not tolerated: the receiver treats a repeated identity at a revision it already holds with a different content digest as `native fact identity conflict`, and passive facts carry capturedAt and sourceGeneration, so a re-read always differs. Exact replay of the same intent bytes is idempotent.

Limits and assumptions: the 24-identity window relies on the Claude writer finishing all content blocks of a response before the next response starts (observed, not a documented contract); a correction to an older response would conflict at the receiver, visibly. Active Codex rollouts keep the original no-retirement rule, so a single Codex rollout with more than 256 responses still stalls until it closes. Records with no timestamp from an unknown source are suppressed once a horizon exists. Tests are synthetic; installed adoption and receiver ingestion (Host built from 61526e94 or later) are separate.
title: A passive telemetry association needs retirement of finished state, or it stalls after a few transcripts
